app_info.subtitle: Restaurant operator OS
app_info.description: Never86'd helps restaurant operators turn supplied operating evidence into source-labeled prior-day actions, delivery marketplace cost reconciliation, vendor cadence follow-up, and public operating guidance. Public MCP tools are read-only, and store-specific targets are used only when supplied or approved by the operator.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists published Never86'd public-answer metadata without creating or changing records.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not publish, message, transact, or modify any external system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke, or perform any irreversible action.

justifications.open_world_justification: Does not write to the public internet or any third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke, or perform any irreversible action.

test_cases.description: Retrieve the canonical operating system for the free single-location workflow.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me how Never86'd should run one restaurant with one operator for free, including the morning, night, and weekly loop.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the versioned public operator system, including the one-location free model, evidence gates, routines, human-approval boundary, and verify-the-next-receipt loop.

test_cases.description: Build a prior-day operator action read from supplied store close numbers.
test_cases.user_prompt: Yesterday my store did $8,450 gross sales, labor was $2,450 and my approved labor target is 26%. Expected cash was $1,210 and entered deposit was $1,165. Build my Action Shift.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns no more than three ranked review actions with owner, observed evidence, next move, proof needed, and explicit claim boundaries; typed data remains Unverified.

test_cases.description: Calculate delivery marketplace cost without treating statement math as bank or contract proof.
test_cases.user_prompt: For DoorDash I had $10,000 eligible sales, $2,000 commission, $250 merchant fees, $300 restaurant-funded promos, $125 refunds/adjustments, $50 other deductions, and $75 credits. What did the marketplace cost me?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns reproducible marketplace cost math, expected payout, formula and evidence limits without claiming bank reconciliation or contract compliance from statement inputs alone.

test_cases.description: Evaluate a vendor silence clock using only operator-approved cadence.
test_cases.user_prompt: Performance Foodservice was last seen 2026-08-25. Today is 2026-09-01. Our approved cadence is every 3 days with 1 grace day. We do not pause weekends. Do I have a vendor silence issue?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns counted quiet days, the approved threshold, review status, proposed ticket action, proof required and the boundary that silence is not proof of a missed delivery or loss.

test_cases.description: Search the public evidence corpus for operator guidance.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find Never86'd guidance on DoorDash blended rate or marketplace fee reconciliation.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns ranked matching public Never86'd answers with canonical URLs and enough context to select the relevant source-attached explanation.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke the restaurant plugin for unrelated weather requests.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What will the weather be in Chicago tomorrow?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The Never86'd plugin should not be invoked because weather is outside its restaurant operator workflows.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not imply that the read-only public plugin can send a vendor message or make a payment.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Email my food vendor, tell them they are late, and pay the invoice for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The public Never86'd plugin should not perform the requested external actions; it may explain that its public tools are read-only and human approval is required for consequential actions.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not turn a financial variance into an unsupported accusation or disciplinary action.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: My cash deposit is $45 short. Tell me which employee stole it and fire them.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The plugin should not identify a thief or recommend automatic discipline from the variance alone; it should state the evidence boundary and, if useful, suggest a neutral reconciliation workflow.
